text:
Jake Sanderson missed the start of the season and has played 17 games, and he's already at 23:20 a night, the minutes of a team's top defenseman. His return was a big enough deal that Graeme Nichols wrote a full analytics piece on what it changed.

The points are coming the patient way: 13 in 17, 12 of them assists, and only one goal on 2.8 expected. He gets to dangerous ice for a defenseman (96th percentile for chances from the slot in Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking), so the goals should come. The Senators take 54% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on. The odd number is relative: about a point worse with him than without, which says more about how good Ottawa has been in his absence. Evolving-Hockey had him fifth among all defensemen in wins above replacement last season. Our range projects 46 to 68 points over the games he has left.
